import subprocess

# Verify: str.split with maxsplit equivalent
code = r'''
# In Python str.split, there's no maxsplit=0 concept directly,
# but in our implementation, maxsplit=0 means "no splitting"
# which returns all values as one chunk

from boltons.iterutils import split

# Test that maxsplit=0 returns all values as one chunk
result = split([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], sep=3, maxsplit=0)
print("maxsplit=0:", result)
assert result == [[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]], f"Expected [[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]], got {result}"

# Compare with maxsplit=1 (one split)
result = split([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], sep=3, maxsplit=1)
print("maxsplit=1:", result)
assert result == [[1, 2], [4, 5]]

print("PASS")
'''
result = subprocess.run(['python', '-c', code], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
print(result.stdout)
